dinesh: Heads up — saw a kernel-picker flip in a small canary on A100s. Batch-level seq=96 mostly picked flash_attn_v2 but ~12% of tokens fell back to sdpa_v1 and p50 jumped.

maria: Any chance this is kv-cache warmup or uneven padding across requests?

dinesh: I dumped the profiler, snippet below:
```
model: llama-13b
device: a100-sxm
batch: 16
seq: 96 (mixed: some 96, some 20 padded)
heads: 16
head_dim: 64
chosen_kernel: flash_attn_v2 (~88% tokens)
fallback_kernel: sdpa_v1 (~12% tokens)
p50 latency: 32ms normal -> 65ms when fallback hits
tokens/s: 38k -> 19k on fallback
notes: fallback tends to trigger on short remainder sequences and when head_dim not multiple of 32 in the selector path
```

jess: I remember a similar symptom when head_dim==48 and our selector heuristics used a tight tiling table. remainder fragments would map to sdpa path.

alex: This smells like two interacting issues: (1) the sequence-length-dependent switch threshold doesn't handle mixed-length batches, (2) the architecture/tiling heuristic treats remainder fragments as incompatibility. We should make the picker aware of batch sequence distribution and kv-cache state.

perf-bot: autotune-run-2026-03-16: summary -> H100: flash_v3 wins for seq<=64, flash_v2 for 65-256, sdpa paths only for head_dim%32 != 0 or non-causal kernels. A100_sxm: flash_v2 preferred for 32-192, sdpa fallback cost penalty ~1.9x on p50.

maria: So actionable: 1) avoid per-request flips if batch contains mixed seq lengths, 2) add a head_dim alignment check earlier, 3) make selector prefer a single safe kernel per batch when kv-cache is present.

dinesh: I'll prototype a conservative batch-level guard: if batch seq stddev > 12 or any seq<32 and any seq>64 -> force flash_attn_v2 (no sdpa). Also add special-case for head_dim 48 to prefer v2. Will run autotune against A100 pool.

jess: I'll add a test that simulates fragmented kv-cache (prefix + many short suffixes) and asserts no sdpa fallbacks for that scenario. Also adding telemetry to record "selector_flip" events when more than 5% of tokens use a different kernel within the same batch.

alex: Can we also log the exact remainder lengths that triggered the fallback? That would help tune tiling thresholds.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment: runtime-selector-v0.7 -> staging started by dinesh at 2026-03-16T18:12:03Z

dinesh: Thanks. If the autotune run on A100 still prefers sdpa for these mixed cases, we'll add an explicit override table keyed by (device_family, head_dim_mod, batch_seq_profile).

maria: :thumbsup: Also flagging perf regression alert if token/sec drops >25% compared to baseline for 1m window.

jess: Note: small, short-lived spikes are fine as long as we avoid sustained 2x regressions caused by kernel flip.

dinesh: Filing a follow-up PR for the selector guard and the new telemetry. Will post results from A100 autotune tomorrow.
